newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Exxel Group to float Argentine utilities - papers.
newsitem.headline: Exxel Group to float Argentine utilities - papers.

text.p: International investment fund and holding The Exxel Group plans to float its three Argentine electricity firms this year as a first step to listing all of its companies, the Clarin newspaper said Friday.
"Our goal is to float all of our companies," Clarin quoted President Juan Navarro as saying at the inauguration of new electrical facilities.
Navarro was quoted by La Nacion as saying, "The electric sector will be the first of our group to be listed."
Clarin said the electricity firms would be listed on the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange before the end of the year, and probably on the New York Stock Exchange.
Exxel controls Edesal, Edelar and Edesa, which distribute power in the Argentine provinces of San Luis, La Rioja and Salta.
"We aim to create a strong electricity distribution regional firm through which we could go to Brazil," La Nacion quoted Navarro as saying.
Clarin reported the group plans to participate in new privatizations in Brazil and Bolivia.

Navarro said the group will not bid in the privatization this year of Buenos Aires Province's Empresa Social de Energa de Buenos Aires SA (ESEBA), which has attracted the interest of 21 Argentine and foreign companies.

Buenos Aires Governor Eduardo Duhalde has said he expects ESEBA to fetch more than $1 billion. Among those interested in ESEBA are Argentina's YPF, Prez Companc, Central Costanera and Sideco, Chile's Enersis, Chilquinta and Sociedad Austral de Electricidad.
Exxel is interested in possibly buying other provincial firms to be privatized as those of Mendoza, Crdoba and Santiago del Estero, La Nacin said.
It invests exclusively in the Mercosur customs union comprising Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
It controls several investment funds in which Rockefeller & Co, The Ford Foundation, The Getty Family Trust, CS First Boston, Crdit Suisse Holdings, General Electric and Oppenheimer & Co have stakes.

In the last four years, Exxel has invested $980 million in Argentina, mostly in private health, energy, restaurant and credit card sectors. It bought 19 companies with total annual revenues of $1.9 billion.
Last year, the group bought Argentine supermarket chain CADESA (Supermercados Norte) for $440 million.
